### §2.6.6 Group `M15-A-VCG06` (id=3639) — H2450 cha.kham

_The term names the inner posture of self-attributed wisdom — wisdom held as personal possession, the inner stance of believing oneself wise. Inner-being phenomenon: self-claim to wisdom. Distinct from VCG03 (settled character) because the verses are not about the constitution of wisdom but about the person's own claim or self-estimation. Distinct from VCG07 because the focus is the individual inner posture, not the worldly category._

**Verses:** 19 connected (1 anchor, 18 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

|---|---|---|---|
| **Pro 26:12** | H2450 cha.kham | Pro 26:12 Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes ? There is more hope for a fool than for him . | "a man who is wise in his own eyes — more hope for a fool" — self-attributed wisdom as worse than foolishness; inner self-assessment as the problem |

### §2.6.7 Group `M15-A-VCG07` (id=3640) — H2450 cha.kham

_The term names the inner orientation that constitutes 'wisdom of this age' or 'wisdom of the world' — overturned by the cross or by divine action. Inner-being phenomenon: the orientation of mind that operates apart from God and is exposed as foolishness. The Pauline cross-wisdom reversal is the centre; OT verses where God renders wise men foolish belong here also. Includes wisdom turned to deceit, cunning, or craftiness directed against truth or against the people of God._

### §2.6.8 Group `M15-A-VCG08` (id=3641) — H2450 cha.kham

_The term names the perceptive inner capacity — the act of grasping meaning, understanding what is heard or read, interpreting what is shown. Inner-being phenomenon: inner intelligibility. Distinct from VCG03 because the focus is on the moment or act of comprehending, not the standing character of the person. The verses describe the inner faculty by which sense is made._

**Verses:** 10 connected (1 anchor, 9 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Neh 8:8** | H0995 bin | Neh 8:8 They read from the book , from the Law of God , clearly , and they gave the sense , so that the people understood the reading . | "they gave the sense so that the people understood the reading" — bin activated by clear exposition; the inner faculty grasps meaning when the word is made clear |

**Other verses related to the context:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Neh 8:8 | H7922 se.khel | Neh 8:8 They read from the book , from the Law of God , clearly , and they gave the sense , so that the people understood the reading . | "gave the sense so the people understood the reading" — se.khel as the quality enabling comprehension to be communicated |
| Job 17:4 | H7922 se.khel | Job 17:4 Since you have closed their hearts to understanding , therefore you will not let them triumph . | "closed their hearts to understanding" — se.khel blocked; the closing of the heart shuts it out |
| Jer 9:12 | H2450 cha.kham | Jer 9:12 Who is the man so wise that he can understand this ? To whom has the mouth of the Lord spoken , that he may declare it? Why is the land ruined and laid waste like a wilderness , so that no one passes through ? | "who is so wise that he can understand this?" — the wise are challenged; wisdom insufficient to comprehend judgment |
| Jer 9:17 | H0995 bin | Jer 9:17 Thus says the Lord of hosts : “ Consider , and call for the mourning women to come ; send for the skillful women to come ; | "Consider, and call for the mourning women" — bin as careful perception in a complex situation |
| Hos 14:9 | H2450 cha.kham | Hos 14:9 Whoever is wise , let him understand these things; whoever is discerning , let him know them; for the ways of the Lord are right , and the upright walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them . | "whoever is wise, let him understand these things" — wisdom as the prerequisite for understanding |
| Hos 14:9 | H0995 bin | Hos 14:9 Whoever is wise , let him understand these things; whoever is discerning , let him know them; for the ways of the Lord are right , and the upright walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them . | "whoever is discerning, let him know them" — bin as what enables recognition of the ways of the Lord |
| Hos 14:9 | H3045 ya.da | Hos 14:9 Whoever is wise , let him understand these things; whoever is discerning , let him know them; for the ways of the Lord are right , and the upright walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them . | "whoever is discerning, let him know them" — knowing the ways of the Lord as the mark of moral discernment |
| Rev 13:18 | G4678 sofia | Rev 13:18 This calls for wisdom : let the one who has understanding calculate the number of the beast , for it is the number of a man , and his number is 666 . | "this calls for wisdom" — appeal to Spirit-given discernment; the wisdom needed cannot be manufactured |
| Rev 17:9 | G4678 sofia | Rev 17:9 This calls for a mind with wisdom : the seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman is seated ; | "this calls for a mind with wisdom" — same pattern: wisdom as a received capacity for reading what is hidden |

### §2.6.11 Group `M15-A-VCG09` (id=3642) — H2450 cha.kham

_The term names wisdom as the inner state that arises from, or is constituted by, the fear of the Lord, attentiveness to God's ways, or the practice of God's law. Inner-being phenomenon: covenantal inner orientation. Distinct from VCG03 (general wise character) because the verses explicitly name fear of the Lord or covenant practice as the source or substance of the wisdom._

**Verses:** 3 connected (1 anchor, 2 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Psa 111:10** | H7922 se.khel | Psa 111:10 The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom ; all those who practice it have a good understanding . His praise endures forever ! | "all who practice it have good understanding" — se.khel as the fruit of practicing the fear of the Lord |

**Other verses related to the context:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deu 4:6 | H2450 cha.kham | Deu 4:6 Keep them and do them, for that will be your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples , who , when they hear all these statutes , will say , ‘ Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people .’ | "wisdom and understanding in the sight of the peoples" — covenant obedience produces visible wisdom; other nations will perceive it as a national quality |
| Mic 6:9 | H8454 tu.shiy.yah | Mic 6:9 The voice of the Lord cries to the city — and it is sound wisdom to fear your name : “ Hear of the rod and of him who appointed it ! | "it is sound wisdom to fear your name" — tu.shiy.yah defined by its content: the fear of the Lord |

### §2.6.12 Group `M15-A-VCG10` (id=3643) — H2803G cha.shav

_The term names the inner act of devising artistic designs for sacred construction — the mental forming of pattern that precedes and directs the physical work. Inner-being phenomenon: inner creative-design capacity for sacred purpose. Restricted to the Exodus verses where 'to devise artistic designs' is named as the activity, in the context of Spirit-given craftsmanship for the tabernacle. Distinct from VCG02 because the focus is on the forming activity rather than the moment of endowment._

**Verses:** 4 connected (1 anchor, 3 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exo 35:32 | H2803G cha.shav | Exo 35:32 to devise artistic designs , to work in gold and silver and bronze , | "to devise artistic designs" |
| Exo 35:35 | H2803G cha.shav | Exo 35:35 He has filled them with skill to do every sort of work done by an engraver or by a designer or by an embroiderer in blue and purple and scarlet yarns and fine twined linen , or by a weaver —by any sort of workman or skilled designer . | "skilled designer" — the person is identified by this inner capacity |
| Exo 38:23 | H2803G cha.shav | Exo 38:23 and with him was Oholiab the son of Ahisamach , of the tribe of Dan , an engraver and designer and embroiderer in blue and purple and scarlet yarns and fine twined linen . | "designer" — inner design capacity as identity |

### §2.6.13 Group `M15-B-VCG01` (id=3644) — H0995 bin

_The term names understanding as belonging to God himself — his self-sufficient, uncreated comprehension of all things. This includes his perceptive knowing of every human heart and plan, his understanding as the faculty by which creation is ordered and sustained, and the explicit assertion that no one gave or taught him understanding. Inner-being phenomenon: divine inner attribute._

### §2.6.16 Group `M15-B-VCG03` (id=3646) — H2450 cha.kham

_The term names understanding as a constituted inner quality that grasps, discerns, and perceives — in leadership, wisdom literature, practical navigation of situations, and the moral life. The person of understanding reads situations rightly, receives instruction, governs speech, sees through pretension, perceives the rights of others, and is responsive to correction. Inner-being phenomenon: the exercise and possession of the perceptive faculty._

### §2.6.17 Group `M15-B-VCG03` (id=3646) — H0995 bin

_The term names understanding as a constituted inner quality that grasps, discerns, and perceives — in leadership, wisdom literature, practical navigation of situations, and the moral life. The person of understanding reads situations rightly, receives instruction, governs speech, sees through pretension, perceives the rights of others, and is responsive to correction. Inner-being phenomenon: the exercise and possession of the perceptive faculty._

### §2.6.18 Group `M15-B-VCG03` (id=3646) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names understanding as a constituted inner quality that grasps, discerns, and perceives — in leadership, wisdom literature, practical navigation of situations, and the moral life. The person of understanding reads situations rightly, receives instruction, governs speech, sees through pretension, perceives the rights of others, and is responsive to correction. Inner-being phenomenon: the exercise and possession of the perceptive faculty._

### §2.6.19 Group `M15-B-VCG04` (id=3647) — H2450 cha.kham

_The term names the inner perceptive faculty by its judicial withholding (God closes it), by its moral blockage (hardened hearts cannot understand), by its absence in a person or community as a sign of their condition, or as a capacity that is present but overwhelmed by what exceeds it. Inner-being phenomenon: the blocked, absent, or overmatched faculty._

**Verses:** 59 connected (1 anchor, 58 other)

### §2.6.20 Group `M15-B-VCG04` (id=3647) — H0995 bin

_The term names the inner perceptive faculty by its judicial withholding (God closes it), by its moral blockage (hardened hearts cannot understand), by its absence in a person or community as a sign of their condition, or as a capacity that is present but overwhelmed by what exceeds it. Inner-being phenomenon: the blocked, absent, or overmatched faculty._

### §2.6.22 Group `M15-B-VCG06` (id=3649) — H0995 bin

_The term names the inner perceptive act of grasping disclosed content — visions, prophetic words, Scripture, and the mystery of Christ. The faculty is engaged specifically with what has been revealed rather than with ordinary practical matters. Understanding here is the successful or sought reception of meaning from God's disclosure. Inner-being phenomenon: inner perceptive reception of revealed content._

### §2.6.23 Group `M15-C-VCG01` (id=3651) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names God's comprehensive, self-sufficient knowing of all things — hearts, plans, character, deeds. No one gave him this knowing; his understanding is unsearchable. Distinct from his elective knowing of persons (VCG02) and his redemptive self-disclosure through acts (VCG03). Inner-being phenomenon: divine omniscient attribute._

### §2.6.24 Group `M15-C-VCG02` (id=3652) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names God's knowing as an act of electing, choosing, and entering into intimate covenantal relationship — face to face knowing, knowing in the wilderness, 'You only have I known of all the families of the earth.' This is not God's omniscient knowing of everyone but his specific relational knowing that constitutes covenant identity. Inner-being phenomenon: divine elective knowing._

### §2.6.25 Group `M15-C-VCG03` (id=3653) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names God's redemptive self-disclosure through historical events — 'that you/they may know that I am the Lord.' The pattern runs through Exodus, the wilderness, the Jordan crossing, the prophets, and the apocalyptic oracles. The goal is always inner recognition produced by the event. Inner-being phenomenon: God's self-revealing disclosure through history._

### §2.6.26 Group `M15-C-VCG04` (id=3654) — H0995 bin

_The term names the human person's relational inner knowing of God — pressing on to know him, finding the knowledge of God, knowing him in the act of doing justice. This is the human side of the covenantal encounter: the person's inner recognition of who God is, sustained by covenant practice. Inner-being phenomenon: human covenantal knowledge of God._

**Verses:** 49 connected (1 anchor, 48 other)

### §2.6.27 Group `M15-C-VCG04` (id=3654) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names the human person's relational inner knowing of God — pressing on to know him, finding the knowledge of God, knowing him in the act of doing justice. This is the human side of the covenantal encounter: the person's inner recognition of who God is, sustained by covenant practice. Inner-being phenomenon: human covenantal knowledge of God._

### §2.6.28 Group `M15-C-VCG05` (id=3655) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names the structural opposite — a person, community, or nation that does not know God, refuses the knowledge of God, or lacks it. The sons of Eli did not know the Lord. Israel has no knowledge of God in the land. The wicked do not desire the knowledge of his ways. Sometimes the absence is culpable refusal; sometimes it is the condition of those outside the covenant. Inner-being phenomenon: absent or refused covenantal knowing._

### §2.6.29 Group `M15-C-VCG06` (id=3656) — H2450 cha.kham

_The term names knowledge as an inner content or capacity possessed, accumulated, guarded, and transmitted — the Proverbs portrait of da.at as a valued inner endowment. The wise lay up knowledge; lips of the wise spread it; knowledge is pleasant to the soul; the prudent guard it. Includes knowledge as the content of wise speech, as God's creative-ordering capacity, and as the transmissible substance of wisdom instruction. Inner-being phenomenon: knowledge as inner content held and exercised._

### §2.6.30 Group `M15-C-VCG06` (id=3656) — H0995 bin

_The term names knowledge as an inner content or capacity possessed, accumulated, guarded, and transmitted — the Proverbs portrait of da.at as a valued inner endowment. The wise lay up knowledge; lips of the wise spread it; knowledge is pleasant to the soul; the prudent guard it. Includes knowledge as the content of wise speech, as God's creative-ordering capacity, and as the transmissible substance of wisdom instruction. Inner-being phenomenon: knowledge as inner content held and exercised._

### §2.6.32 Group `M15-C-VCG07` (id=3657) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names the specifically moral knowing that distinguishes good from evil — named in the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, acquired through the fall, withheld from moral infants, and called for as a developmental marker. This is knowing as a moral-discriminating capacity: the person who can distinguish right from wrong, choose the good, refuse the evil. Inner-being phenomenon: moral discriminating knowledge._

### §2.6.33 Group `M15-C-VCG08` (id=3658) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names knowing as a settled inner conviction — the 'we know that' pattern of the Pauline letters; Job's sustained convictions about God, his situation, and his Redeemer; Qoheleth's recognitions about what he has perceived. The phenomenon is not the relational knowing of God (VCG04) but the inner state of holding something as certain. Inner-being phenomenon: inner certainty or conviction._

### §2.6.34 Group `M15-C-VCG09` (id=3659) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names ignorance that is culpable, structural, or judicially significant — the agnoeō (G0050) pattern: those who do not know because they have not perceived, those whose ignorance becomes the mechanism of their actions, those Paul corrects by disclosure. Includes innocent ignorance where the absence rather than the culpability is what the term names. Inner-being phenomenon: inner state of ignorance with moral or judicial significance._

### §2.6.36 Group `M15-C-VCG10` (id=3660) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names the ordinary, practical knowing of persons, facts, situations, and skills — knowing where someone went, knowing that a person is trustworthy, knowing a skill, recognising someone. This is knowing as everyday awareness and competence, not covenantal or moral. The largest group by verse count, spanning narrative throughout Genesis–Malachi and the NT. Inner-being phenomenon: practical inner awareness and recognition._

### §2.6.37 Group `M15-C-VCG11` (id=3661) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names sexual union through the verb 'to know' — the Hebraic expression of the deepest intimacy between persons. Includes positive descriptions of marital union, statements of virginity ('had not known a man'), and instances of sexual violation. The phenomenon is intimate union — the most personal form of human knowing — expressed through the same verb that names all other forms of knowing. Inner-being phenomenon: intimate union as knowing._

### §2.6.38 Group `M15-C-VCG12` (id=3662) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names the universal knowing of God that marks the end of history — 'the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea.' This is not the present covenantal knowing of the faithful few but the future universal inner knowing of all creation. Inner-being phenomenon: eschatological universal knowing._

**Verses:** 2 connected (1 anchor, 1 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hab 2:14** | H3045 ya.da | Hab 2:14 For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord as the waters cover the sea . | "earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord" — eschatological covenantal knowing filling all creation |

**Other verses related to the context:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|

### §2.6.39 Group `M15-D-VCG01` (id=3663) — H0995 bin

_The term names the inner quality of prudent wisdom as it generates effective, God-aligned action — success in conduct, perceptive discernment of one's path, wise attending to God's acts, the eschatological wisdom of Daniel's wise ones who shine. The phenomenon is wisdom not as abstract capacity but as engaged, productive inner discernment that shapes conduct and its outcomes. Inner-being phenomenon: prudent discernment expressed in action._

### §2.6.40 Group `M15-D-VCG01` (id=3663) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names the inner quality of prudent wisdom as it generates effective, God-aligned action — success in conduct, perceptive discernment of one's path, wise attending to God's acts, the eschatological wisdom of Daniel's wise ones who shine. The phenomenon is wisdom not as abstract capacity but as engaged, productive inner discernment that shapes conduct and its outcomes. Inner-being phenomenon: prudent discernment expressed in action._

**Verses:** 69 connected (1 anchor, 68 other)

### §2.6.41 Group `M15-D-VCG03` (id=3665) — H2803H cha.shav

_The term names the inner act of crediting, imputing, or reckoning — whether divine (counting faith as righteousness, not imputing iniquity) or human (regarding others as foreigners, esteeming the Servant's name). The phenomenon is evaluation that produces a moral standing or classification. Inner-being phenomenon: evaluative reckoning that assigns worth or guilt._

**Anchor verse:**

### §2.6.42 Group `M15-D-VCG04` (id=3666) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names the inner deliberative act of thinking — forming an assessment through attending to evidence or reflection. Includes: Judah forming a wrong judgment from observation, Eli misreading Hannah's posture, Job's friends' inner evaluations of him, the psalmist struggling to think through the wicked's prosperity, pondering past divine acts, and the contemplative attending to one's own ways. Inner-being phenomenon: deliberate inner cognitive formation of a judgment._

### §2.6.43 Group `M15-D-VCG05` (id=3667) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names tasting as the figure for inner discernment — the palate that tests food becomes the image for the inner faculty that tests words, situations, and God himself. Includes literal tasting (Jonathan's honey, Nineveh's fast, mourning abstinence), and figurative tasting (taste and see that the Lord is good; the ear tests words as the palate tastes food). Inner-being phenomenon: taste as the organ of inner discernment._

### §2.6.44 Group `M15-D-VCG06` (id=3668) — H2450 cha.kham

_The term names the inner quality of shrewd perceptiveness that can be either wisdom or cunning depending on its direction. The serpent is crafty (a.rum) — the same word that describes the prudent person who sees danger and hides, conceals knowledge, and gives thought to steps. The phenomenon is a sharp, discerning inner disposition that either serves wisdom or serves deception. Inner-being phenomenon: shrewd inner discernment as double-edged disposition._

**Verses:** 15 connected (1 anchor, 14 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|

He said to the woman , “Did God actually say , ‘You shall not eat of any tree in the garden ’?” | "the serpent was more crafty" — a.rum in its dark register; the same shrewdness serving deception |

### §2.6.46 Group `M15-E-VCG01` (id=3670) — G1014 boulomai

_The term names the inner volitional act of purposive willing — Joseph's resolution to divorce Mary quietly, Pilate's will to satisfy the crowd, Christ's sovereign will to disclose the Father, the Spirit's will in distributing gifts, God's will that none should perish. The phenomenon is the inner act of forming and holding a deliberate intention. Inner-being phenomenon: purposive volitional willing._

### §2.6.49 Group `M15-E-VCG02` (id=3671) — G1106 gnōmē

_The term names the inner considered resolution — Paul's deliberate judgment offered without a dominical command, the collective resolution that unites or divides a community, the unified purpose God places in the hearts of the hostile kings. The phenomenon is a formed inner judgment held as a resolution rather than an impulse. Inner-being phenomenon: considered inner resolution._

**Verses:** 8 connected (1 anchor, 7 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rev 17:17** | G1106 gnōmē | Rev 17:17 for God has put it into their hearts to carry out his purpose by being of one mind and handing over their royal power to the beast , until the words of God are fulfilled . | "God has put it into their hearts to carry out his purpose... until the words of God are fulfilled" — gnōmē divinely placed; human deliberate purpose as instrument of divine sovereignty |

**Other verses related to the context:**

|---|---|---|---|

| 1Cor 1:10 | G1106 gnōmē | 1Cor 1:10 I appeal to you , brothers , by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ , that all of you agree , and that there be no divisions among you , but that you be united in the same mind and the same judgment . | "united in the same mind and the same judgment" — gnōmē as the shared deliberate position; basis of communal unity |

### §2.6.50 Group `M15-E-VCG03` (id=3672) — H3289 ya.ats

_The term names the divine counsel as irresistible sovereign intent — 'as I have planned, so shall it be; as I have purposed, so shall it stand' (Isa 14:24). God's ya.ats is unalterable: no one counselled him (Isa 40:14), his counsel against nations will stand, and the Messiah is the Wonderful Counselor whose inner wisdom directs his people. Inner-being phenomenon: divine sovereign purposive counsel._

### §2.6.51 Group `M15-E-VCG04` (id=3673) — H2450 cha.kham

_The term names the human counseling relationship — advisors sought, wisdom given, counsel rejected or followed, the counselor role as the expression of inner wisdom in the service of governance. Includes good counsel (Jethro, Hushai's counter-counsel), wicked counsel (Ahab's house), hostile counsel (enemies conspiring), and the prophetic refusal to give counsel when it will not be heard. Inner-being phenomenon: purposive wisdom given and received between persons._

### §2.6.52 Group `M15-E-VCG04` (id=3673) — H3289 ya.ats

_The term names the human counseling relationship — advisors sought, wisdom given, counsel rejected or followed, the counselor role as the expression of inner wisdom in the service of governance. Includes good counsel (Jethro, Hushai's counter-counsel), wicked counsel (Ahab's house), hostile counsel (enemies conspiring), and the prophetic refusal to give counsel when it will not be heard. Inner-being phenomenon: purposive wisdom given and received between persons._

### §2.6.54 Group `M15-E-VCG04` (id=3673) — H0995 bin

_The term names the human counseling relationship — advisors sought, wisdom given, counsel rejected or followed, the counselor role as the expression of inner wisdom in the service of governance. Includes good counsel (Jethro, Hushai's counter-counsel), wicked counsel (Ahab's house), hostile counsel (enemies conspiring), and the prophetic refusal to give counsel when it will not be heard. Inner-being phenomenon: purposive wisdom given and received between persons._

**Verses:** 66 connected (1 anchor, 65 other)

### §2.6.55 Group `M15-E-VCG04` (id=3673) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names the human counseling relationship — advisors sought, wisdom given, counsel rejected or followed, the counselor role as the expression of inner wisdom in the service of governance. Includes good counsel (Jethro, Hushai's counter-counsel), wicked counsel (Ahab's house), hostile counsel (enemies conspiring), and the prophetic refusal to give counsel when it will not be heard. Inner-being phenomenon: purposive wisdom given and received between persons._

### §2.6.56 Group `M15-E-VCG05` (id=3674) — H2803I cha.shav

_The term names deliberate purposive devising — the forming of plans in the heart, whether for good (Pro 16:9 the heart plans its way) or for evil (schemes formed on the bed, Mic 2:1; Ezekiel's men devising wickedness; the Assyrian king's destructive intent). God also devises — disaster against those who devised wickedness, plans for welfare in Jer 29:11. Inner-being phenomenon: purposive plan-forming in the inner person._

### §2.6.57 Group `M15-E-VCG05` (id=3674) — H6191 a.rom

_The term names deliberate purposive devising — the forming of plans in the heart, whether for good (Pro 16:9 the heart plans its way) or for evil (schemes formed on the bed, Mic 2:1; Ezekiel's men devising wickedness; the Assyrian king's destructive intent). God also devises — disaster against those who devised wickedness, plans for welfare in Jer 29:11. Inner-being phenomenon: purposive plan-forming in the inner person._

### §2.6.58 Group `M15-E-VCG06` (id=3675) — H2161 za.mam

_The term names purpose so firmly resolved that it cannot be revoked — human unified purposing (Gen 11:6, Tower of Babel), and divine irrevocable decisions (Jer 4:28, Jer 51:12, Lam 2:17). The phenomenon is the inner intentional act at its most fixed: what has been za.mam-ed has been purposed and will not be relented from. Inner-being phenomenon: irrevocable inner resolving._

**Verses:** 4 connected (1 anchor, 3 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lam 2:17** | H2161 za.mam | Lam 2:17 The Lord has done what he purposed ; he has carried out his word , which he commanded long ago ; he has thrown down without pity ; he has made the enemy rejoice over you and exalted the might of your foes . | "the Lord has done what he purposed" — divine za.mam fulfilled in Jerusalem's fall |

**Other verses related to the context:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gen 11:6 | H2161 za.mam | Gen 11:6 And the Lord said , “Behold, they are one people , and they have all one language , and this is only the beginning of what they will do . And nothing that they propose to do will now be impossible for them. | "nothing they propose will be impossible" — za.mam as unified deliberate human purposing |
| Jer 4:28 | H2161 za.mam | Jer 4:28 “ For this the earth shall mourn , and the heavens above be dark ; for I have spoken ; I have purposed ; I have not relented , nor will I turn back .” | "I have spoken; I have purposed; I have not relented, nor will I turn back" — divine za.mam as irrevocable |
| Jer 51:12 | H2161 za.mam | Jer 51:12 “Set up a standard against the walls of Babylon ; make the watch strong ; set up watchmen ; prepare the ambushes ; for the Lord has both planned and done what he spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon . | "the Lord has both planned and done what he spoke" — za.mam executed; divine purpose becoming historical fact |

### §2.6.59 Group `M15-E-VCG07` (id=3676) — H7896K shit

_The term names the deliberate act of directing the heart's attention — setting the heart toward something, or the failure to do so. Pharaoh deliberately does not set his heart to the signs; the dying woman cannot set her attention to what is said; Absalom counsels Tamar not to set her heart to what happened; the psalmist takes counsel in his soul. Inner-being phenomenon: the deliberate directing of inner attention._

**Verses:** 7 connected (1 anchor, 6 other)

|---|---|---|---|

### §2.6.60 Group `M15-E-VCG08` (id=3677) — H3045 ya.da

_The term names the inner capacity for purposive foresight — the governor's capacity to plan for his community's welfare (pronoia), the person who makes provision for the flesh's desires, Qoheleth's quest for the rational scheme of things (chesh.bon), thought as a capacity belonging only to the living, and the divine inner attending being appealed to by a desperate captain. Inner-being phenomenon: rational planning capacity and purposive foresight._

### §2.6.62 Group `M15-E-VCG08` (id=3677) — G4307 pronoia

_The term names the inner capacity for purposive foresight — the governor's capacity to plan for his community's welfare (pronoia), the person who makes provision for the flesh's desires, Qoheleth's quest for the rational scheme of things (chesh.bon), thought as a capacity belonging only to the living, and the divine inner attending being appealed to by a desperate captain. Inner-being phenomenon: rational planning capacity and purposive foresight._

### §2.6.65 Group `M15-F-VCG03` (id=3680) — H0995 bin

_The term names the sustained inner activity of meditation — dwelling on God's precepts, pondering his mighty acts, musing until the heart burns, the heart's meditation offered as worship. The meditative inner life is directed toward God's word and works, producing understanding, praise, and orientation through distress. Inner-being phenomenon: sustained inward meditative dwelling._

## §2.7 `M15-F` — Meditative and reflective inner activity

_Terms that name the inner turning of the mind on received material — musing, pondering, the inner dialogue of self-reasoning, and the contemplative considering of a person before God. Activity-oriented (distinct from static thought-content)._

1. Terms in sub-group (14): G1260 dialogizomai, G1261 dialogismos, G1760 enthumeomai, G1761 enthumēsis, H0995 bin, H1900 ha.gut, H1901 ha.gig, H1902H hig.ga.von, H7808 se.ach, H7878 si.ach, H7881 si.chah, H7919A sa.khal, H7920 se.khal, H8394 te.vu.nah
2. Verse-context groups in sub-group (31):

### §2.7.1 Group `M15-A-VCG08` (id=3641) — H0995 bin

_The term names the perceptive inner capacity — the act of grasping meaning, understanding what is heard or read, interpreting what is shown. Inner-being phenomenon: inner intelligibility. Distinct from VCG03 because the focus is on the moment or act of comprehending, not the standing character of the person. The verses describe the inner faculty by which sense is made._

**Verses:** 10 connected (1 anchor, 9 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Neh 8:8** | H0995 bin | Neh 8:8 They read from the book , from the Law of God , clearly , and they gave the sense , so that the people understood the reading . | "they gave the sense so that the people understood the reading" — bin activated by clear exposition; the inner faculty grasps meaning when the word is made clear |

**Other verses related to the context:**

|---|---|---|---|

| Jer 9:17 | H0995 bin | Jer 9:17 Thus says the Lord of hosts : “ Consider , and call for the mourning women to come ; send for the skillful women to come ; | "Consider, and call for the mourning women" — bin as careful perception in a complex situation |

### §2.7.2 Group `M15-B-VCG01` (id=3644) — H8394 te.vu.nah

_The term names understanding as belonging to God himself — his self-sufficient, uncreated comprehension of all things. This includes his perceptive knowing of every human heart and plan, his understanding as the faculty by which creation is ordered and sustained, and the explicit assertion that no one gave or taught him understanding. Inner-being phenomenon: divine inner attribute._

He does not faint or grow weary ; his understanding is unsearchable . | "his understanding is unsearchable" — te.vu.nah as inaccessible to human probing |

### §2.7.4 Group `M15-B-VCG02` (id=3645) — H8394 te.vu.nah

_The term names understanding as a divinely given inner endowment placed into a specific person — Solomon receiving it in answer to prayer, the sanctuary craftsmen filled with the Spirit of understanding and intelligence, Daniel given understanding in visions, Gabriel sent to produce understanding in Daniel, the Messiah anointed with the Spirit of understanding. Inner-being phenomenon: received inner capacity._

### §2.7.6 Group `M15-B-VCG03` (id=3646) — H8394 te.vu.nah

_The term names understanding as a constituted inner quality that grasps, discerns, and perceives — in leadership, wisdom literature, practical navigation of situations, and the moral life. The person of understanding reads situations rightly, receives instruction, governs speech, sees through pretension, perceives the rights of others, and is responsive to correction. Inner-being phenomenon: the exercise and possession of the perceptive faculty._

### §2.7.7 Group `M15-B-VCG03` (id=3646) — H0995 bin

_The term names understanding as a constituted inner quality that grasps, discerns, and perceives — in leadership, wisdom literature, practical navigation of situations, and the moral life. The person of understanding reads situations rightly, receives instruction, governs speech, sees through pretension, perceives the rights of others, and is responsive to correction. Inner-being phenomenon: the exercise and possession of the perceptive faculty._

### §2.7.8 Group `M15-B-VCG04` (id=3647) — H8394 te.vu.nah

_The term names the inner perceptive faculty by its judicial withholding (God closes it), by its moral blockage (hardened hearts cannot understand), by its absence in a person or community as a sign of their condition, or as a capacity that is present but overwhelmed by what exceeds it. Inner-being phenomenon: the blocked, absent, or overmatched faculty._

### §2.7.10 Group `M15-B-VCG04` (id=3647) — G1260 dialogizomai

_The term names the inner perceptive faculty by its judicial withholding (God closes it), by its moral blockage (hardened hearts cannot understand), by its absence in a person or community as a sign of their condition, or as a capacity that is present but overwhelmed by what exceeds it. Inner-being phenomenon: the blocked, absent, or overmatched faculty._

### §2.7.11 Group `M15-B-VCG06` (id=3649) — H0995 bin

_The term names the inner perceptive act of grasping disclosed content — visions, prophetic words, Scripture, and the mystery of Christ. The faculty is engaged specifically with what has been revealed rather than with ordinary practical matters. Understanding here is the successful or sought reception of meaning from God's disclosure. Inner-being phenomenon: inner perceptive reception of revealed content._

### §2.7.12 Group `M15-C-VCG04` (id=3654) — H0995 bin

_The term names the human person's relational inner knowing of God — pressing on to know him, finding the knowledge of God, knowing him in the act of doing justice. This is the human side of the covenantal encounter: the person's inner recognition of who God is, sustained by covenant practice. Inner-being phenomenon: human covenantal knowledge of God._

### §2.7.13 Group `M15-C-VCG05` (id=3655) — H8394 te.vu.nah

_The term names the structural opposite — a person, community, or nation that does not know God, refuses the knowledge of God, or lacks it. The sons of Eli did not know the Lord. Israel has no knowledge of God in the land. The wicked do not desire the knowledge of his ways. Sometimes the absence is culpable refusal; sometimes it is the condition of those outside the covenant. Inner-being phenomenon: absent or refused covenantal knowing._

### §2.7.14 Group `M15-C-VCG06` (id=3656) — H0995 bin

_The term names knowledge as an inner content or capacity possessed, accumulated, guarded, and transmitted — the Proverbs portrait of da.at as a valued inner endowment. The wise lay up knowledge; lips of the wise spread it; knowledge is pleasant to the soul; the prudent guard it. Includes knowledge as the content of wise speech, as God's creative-ordering capacity, and as the transmissible substance of wisdom instruction. Inner-being phenomenon: knowledge as inner content held and exercised._

### §2.7.15 Group `M15-D-VCG01` (id=3663) — H7919A sa.khal

_The term names the inner quality of prudent wisdom as it generates effective, God-aligned action — success in conduct, perceptive discernment of one's path, wise attending to God's acts, the eschatological wisdom of Daniel's wise ones who shine. The phenomenon is wisdom not as abstract capacity but as engaged, productive inner discernment that shapes conduct and its outcomes. Inner-being phenomenon: prudent discernment expressed in action._

### §2.7.16 Group `M15-D-VCG01` (id=3663) — H0995 bin

_The term names the inner quality of prudent wisdom as it generates effective, God-aligned action — success in conduct, perceptive discernment of one's path, wise attending to God's acts, the eschatological wisdom of Daniel's wise ones who shine. The phenomenon is wisdom not as abstract capacity but as engaged, productive inner discernment that shapes conduct and its outcomes. Inner-being phenomenon: prudent discernment expressed in action._

### §2.7.17 Group `M15-E-VCG04` (id=3673) — H0995 bin

_The term names the human counseling relationship — advisors sought, wisdom given, counsel rejected or followed, the counselor role as the expression of inner wisdom in the service of governance. Includes good counsel (Jethro, Hushai's counter-counsel), wicked counsel (Ahab's house), hostile counsel (enemies conspiring), and the prophetic refusal to give counsel when it will not be heard. Inner-being phenomenon: purposive wisdom given and received between persons._

### §2.7.18 Group `M15-F-VCG01` (id=3678) — G1261 dialogismos

_The term names inner deliberative reasoning — questioning in the heart, calculating political consequences, reasoning within oneself in an interior monologue, and the evil thoughts that arise from the heart and produce sinful action. Jesus regularly perceives and names this inner deliberating; the dialogismos of the heart is the site of both corrupt reasoning and honest questioning. Inner-being phenomenon: inner deliberative reasoning._

**Verses:** 27 connected (1 anchor, 26 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Luk 5:22** | G1260 dialogizomai | Luk 5:22 When Jesus perceived their thoughts , he answered them , “ Why do you question in your hearts ? | 'why do you question in your hearts?' — Jesus naming the heart-location |

### §2.7.20 Group `M15-F-VCG02` (id=3679) — G1761 enthumēsis

_The term names sustained inner reflection that produces conceived thoughts — Joseph contemplating his situation before the angel appears, Peter pondering the vision before the Spirit speaks, the Pharisees thinking evil in their hearts, and the formed inner thoughts that the word of God discerns. The phenomenon is the inner conceiving activity that generates thought-content. Inner-being phenomenon: inner reflective conceiving of thought._

**Verses:** 7 connected (1 anchor, 6 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Heb 4:12** | G1761 enthumēsis | Heb 4:12 For the word of God is living and active , sharper than any two-edged sword , piercing to the division of soul and of spirit , of joints and of marrow , and discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart . | 'discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart' — enthumesis (arising) paired with and distinguished from ennoia (held) |

**Other verses related to the context:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mat 1:20 | G1760 enthumeomai | Mat 1:20 But as he considered these things , behold , an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream , saying , “ Joseph , son of David , do not fear to take Mary as your wife , for that which is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit . | 'as he considered these things' — Joseph turning the problem over in his mind before the angel intervenes |
| Mat 9:4 | G1761 enthumēsis | Mat 9:4 But Jesus , knowing their thoughts , said , “ Why do you think evil in your hearts ? | 'knowing their thoughts' — enthumesis as the arising thoughts in the scribes' hearts that Jesus knows |
| Mat 9:4 | G1760 enthumeomai | Mat 9:4 But Jesus , knowing their thoughts , said , “ Why do you think evil in your hearts ? | 'why do you think evil in your hearts?' — Jesus naming the enthumeomai of the scribes; visible to him |
| Mat 12:25 | G1761 enthumēsis | Mat 12:25 Knowing their thoughts , he said to them , “ Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste , and no city or house divided against itself will stand . | 'knowing their thoughts, he said to them' — enthumesis perceived before voiced |
| Act 10:19 | G1760 enthumeomai | Act 10:19 And while Peter was pondering the vision , the Spirit said to him , “ Behold , three men are looking for you . | 'while Peter was pondering the vision, the Spirit said to him' |
| Act 17:29 | G1761 enthumēsis | Act 17:29 Being then God’s offspring , we ought not to think that the divine being is like gold or silver or stone , an image formed by the art and imagination of man . | 'an image formed by the art and imagination of man' — enthumesis as generative inner imagination; here wrongly applied to conceiving the divine |

### §2.7.22 Group `M15-F-VCG03` (id=3680) — H7878 si.ach

_The term names the sustained inner activity of meditation — dwelling on God's precepts, pondering his mighty acts, musing until the heart burns, the heart's meditation offered as worship. The meditative inner life is directed toward God's word and works, producing understanding, praise, and orientation through distress. Inner-being phenomenon: sustained inward meditative dwelling._

|---|---|---|---|

### §2.7.26 Group `M15-F-VCG03` (id=3680) — H0995 bin

_The term names the sustained inner activity of meditation — dwelling on God's precepts, pondering his mighty acts, musing until the heart burns, the heart's meditation offered as worship. The meditative inner life is directed toward God's word and works, producing understanding, praise, and orientation through distress. Inner-being phenomenon: sustained inward meditative dwelling._

### §2.7.29 Group `M15-F-VCG03` (id=3680) — H1902H hig.ga.von

_The term names the sustained inner activity of meditation — dwelling on God's precepts, pondering his mighty acts, musing until the heart burns, the heart's meditation offered as worship. The meditative inner life is directed toward God's word and works, producing understanding, praise, and orientation through distress. Inner-being phenomenon: sustained inward meditative dwelling._

### §2.7.30 Group `M15-F-VCG04` (id=3681) — H7808 se.ach

_The term names either Daniel's focused contemplative attention directed at the revelatory vision (se.khal), or the divine knowing and declaring of what is in the creature's thought (se.ach in Amos 4:13). The phenomenon is either the intense contemplative attending of the person in a revelatory context, or the divine penetrating awareness of human inner thought. Inner-being phenomenon: concentrated contemplation or divine attending to inner thought._

**Verses:** 2 connected (1 anchor, 1 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dan 7:8** | H7920 se.khal | Dan 7:8 I considered the horns , and behold , there came up among them another horn , a little one, before which three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots . And behold , in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man , and a mouth speaking great things . | 'I considered the horns' — se.khal as sustained inner contemplation of the visionary scene; distinct from wisdom/prudence uses in M15-A |

**Other verses related to the context:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amo 4:13 | H7808 se.ach | Amo 4:13 For behold , he who forms the mountains and creates the wind , and declares to man what is his thought , who makes the morning darkness , and treads on the heights of the earth — the Lord , the God of hosts , is his name ! | 'declares to man what is his thought' — God revealing the content of human inner thought-life; the inner is made transparent by divine declaration |

## §2.8 `M15-G` — Inner thought-content — the mind's formed thoughts

_Terms that name the formed thoughts held within the mind — inner content as objects held, which can be guarded, captured, led astray, or disclosed. Static (distinct from reflective activity)._

1. Terms in sub-group (10): G1270 dianoēma, G1771 ennoia, G1963 epinoia, G3540 noēma, G5424 frēn, H4093 mad.da, H6248 ash.tut, H6250 esh.to.nah, H7454 re.a, H7476 ra.yon
2. Verse-context groups in sub-group (10):

### §2.8.1 Group `M15-G-VCG01` (id=3682) — G3540 noēma

_The term names the inner cognitive content — the mind's formed thoughts as they can be blinded, captured, corrupted, or guarded. Satan has designs (noēmata); unbelievers' minds are blinded (noēmata); every thought must be taken captive (noēma); the word of God discerns the intentions and thoughts of the heart (ennoia/enthumēsis); Simon's intent (epinoia) requires repentance. Inner-being phenomenon: formed inner thought-content and cognitive disposition._

**Verses:** 11 connected (1 anchor, 10 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **2Cor 4:4** | G3540 noēma | 2Cor 4:4 In their case the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelievers , to keep them from seeing the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ , who is the image of God . | 'the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelievers' — noema as what is spiritually blinded; the inner formed thought-content that cannot see the gospel |

**Other verses related to the context:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Luk 11:17 | G1270 dianoēma | Luk 11:17 But he , knowing their thoughts , said to them , “ Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste , and a divided household falls . | 'knowing their thoughts, he said to them' — dianoema as the inner formed thoughts of the crowd; Jesus perceives them immediately and responds to their content before they are voiced |
| Act 8:22 | G1963 epinoia | Act 8:22 Repent , therefore , of this wickedness of yours , and pray to the Lord that, if possible , the intent of your heart may be forgiven you . | 'pray to the Lord that, if possible, the intent of your heart may be forgiven you' — epinoia as the heart-located formed intention; explicitly requiring divine forgiveness; the inner design stands as a moral object before God |
| 1Cor 14:20 | G5424 frēn | 1Cor 14:20 Brothers , do not be children in your thinking . Be infants in evil , but in your thinking be mature . | 'do not be children in your thinking. Be infants in evil, but in your thinking be mature' — fren as the inner thinking-capacity with a maturity spectrum; believers are called to its full development |
| 2Cor 2:11 | G3540 noēma | 2Cor 2:11 so that we would not be outwitted by Satan ; for we are not ignorant of his designs . | 'we are not ignorant of his designs' — noema as Satan's formed inner thought-designs; the enemy has a noema that Paul is aware of |
| 2Cor 3:14 | G3540 noēma | 2Cor 3:14 But their minds were hardened . For to this day , when they read the old covenant , that same veil remains unlifted , because only through Christ is it taken away . | 'their minds were hardened' — noema as the cognitive-content capacity that can be hardened; the veil of the old covenant operates on the noema |
| 2Cor 10:5 | G3540 noēma | 2Cor 10:5 We destroy arguments and every lofty opinion raised against the knowledge of God , and take every thought captive to obey Christ , | 'take every thought captive to obey Christ' — noema as the object of spiritual warfare; must be actively captured and submitted |
| 2Cor 11:3 | G3540 noēma | 2Cor 11:3 But I am afraid that as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning , your thoughts will be led astray from a sincere and pure devotion to Christ . | 'your thoughts will be led astray from a sincere and pure devotion to Christ' — noema as the inner thought-content vulnerable to being drawn away from devotion; the serpent's strategy |
| Phili 4:7 | G3540 noēma | Phili 4:7 And the peace of God , which surpasses all understanding , will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus . | 'the peace of God will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus' — noema paired with kardia as the dual objects of divine peace-guarding; the peace of God is the counter to all that would harden, blind, or lead the noema astray |
| Heb 4:12 | G1771 ennoia | Heb 4:12 For the word of God is living and active , sharper than any two-edged sword , piercing to the division of soul and of spirit , of joints and of marrow , and discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart . | 'discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart' — ennoia as the held intentions of the heart; distinguished from enthumesis (arising thoughts); the word of God sees both |
| 1Pe 4:1 | G1771 ennoia | 1Pe 4:1 Since therefore Christ suffered in the flesh , arm yourselves with the same way of thinking , for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin , | 'arm yourselves with the same way of thinking, for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin' — ennoia as the inner held intention that functions as armour; adopting Christ's ennoia re-orientates the inner life away from sin |

### §2.8.4 Group `M15-G-VCG01` (id=3682) — G1963 epinoia

_The term names the inner cognitive content — the mind's formed thoughts as they can be blinded, captured, corrupted, or guarded. Satan has designs (noēmata); unbelievers' minds are blinded (noēmata); every thought must be taken captive (noēma); the word of God discerns the intentions and thoughts of the heart (ennoia/enthumēsis); Simon's intent (epinoia) requires repentance. Inner-being phenomenon: formed inner thought-content and cognitive disposition._

**Verses:** 11 connected (1 anchor, 10 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|

### §2.8.6 Group `M15-G-VCG02` (id=3683) — H6248 ash.tut

_The term names the formed thoughts that arise in the mind — Nebuchadnezzar's night-thoughts producing his dream, Belshazzar's alarming thoughts at the writing on the wall, Daniel's alarming thoughts held inwardly after the vision, God discerning the psalmist's thoughts from afar, and the precious thoughts of God himself. Inner-being phenomenon: arising formed thought-content._

**Verses:** 10 connected (1 anchor, 9 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Psa 139:17** | H7454 re.a | Psa 139:17 How precious to me are your thoughts , O God ! How vast is the sum of them! | 'How precious to me are your thoughts, O God! How vast is the sum of them!' — re.a of God's thoughts toward the human; the same term now runs in the opposite direction; reciprocal |

**Other verses related to the context:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Job 12:5 | H6248 ash.tut | Job 12:5 In the thought of one who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune ; it is ready for those whose feet slip . | 'In the thought of one who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune' — ash.tut as the formed inner thought of the comfortable person; contempt is its content |
| Psa 139:2 | H7454 re.a | Psa 139:2 You know when I sit down and when I rise up ; you discern my thoughts from afar . | 'you discern my thoughts from afar' — re.a as human inner thought-content fully known to God even at distance |
| Psa 146:4 | H6250 esh.to.nah | Psa 146:4 When his breath departs , he returns to the earth ; on that very day his plans perish . | 'when his breath departs, he returns to the earth; on that very day his plans perish' — esh.to.nah as inner plans/thoughts whose existence is entirely dependent on the living breath; at death, they vanish |
| Dan 2:29 | H7476 ra.yon | Dan 2:29 To you , O king , as you lay in bed came thoughts of what would be after this , and he who reveals mysteries made known to you what is to be . | 'as you lay in bed came thoughts of what would be after this' — ra.yon as thoughts arising spontaneously during sleep; the context of royal anxiety about the future |
| Dan 2:30 | H7476 ra.yon | Dan 2:30 But as for me , this mystery has been revealed to me, not because of any wisdom that I have more than all the living , but in order that the interpretation may be made known to the king , and that you may know the thoughts of your mind . | 'that you may know the thoughts of your mind' — ra.yon of the le.vav (heart/mind); the king's formed inner thoughts about what will come |
| Dan 4:19 | H7476 ra.yon | Dan 4:19 Then Daniel , whose name was Belteshazzar , was dismayed for a while , and his thoughts alarmed him. The king answered and said , “ Belteshazzar , let not the dream or the interpretation alarm you.” Belteshazzar answered and said , “My lord , may the dream be for those who hate you and its interpretation for your enemies ! | 'his thoughts alarmed him' — ra.yon producing an inner alarm state in Daniel before he speaks; the thought-content is emotionally active |
| Dan 5:6 | H7476 ra.yon | Dan 5:6 Then the king’s color changed , and his thoughts alarmed him; his limbs gave way , and his knees knocked together . | 'his thoughts alarmed him; his limbs gave way, and his knees knocked together' — ra.yon triggering full somatic cascade: thought -> alarm -> bodily collapse |
| Dan 5:10 | H7476 ra.yon | Dan 5:10 The queen , because of the words of the king and his lords , came into the banqueting hall , and the queen declared , “O king , live forever ! Let not your thoughts alarm you or your color change . | 'let not your thoughts alarm you or your color change' — queen naming ra.yon as the cause of the king's visible distress; inner thoughts shown as visible through their somatic effects |
| Dan 7:28 | H7476 ra.yon | Dan 7:28 “ Here is the end of the matter . As for me , Daniel , my thoughts greatly alarmed me, and my color changed , but I kept the matter in my heart .” | 'my thoughts greatly alarmed me, and my color changed, but I kept the matter in my heart' — ra.yon plus changed colour plus the deliberate act of keeping the content in the le.vav; the thought is felt in the body but held in the heart |

### §2.8.10 Group `M15-G-VCG03` (id=3684) — H4093 mad.da

_The term names knowledge as formed inner content — what Solomon requested from God (wisdom and knowledge), what God placed in the four Danielic youths, what is active even in private thoughts. The phenomenon is knowledge as an inner formed content that can be given by God, held within the person, and exercised in service of governance and wisdom. Inner-being phenomenon: formed inner knowledge-content._

**Verses:** 6 connected (1 anchor, 5 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **2Ch 1:11** | H4093 mad.da | 2Ch 1:11 God answered Solomon , “ Because this was in your heart , and you have not asked for possessions , wealth , honor , or the life of those who hate you, and have not even asked for long life , but have asked for wisdom and knowledge for yourself that you may govern my people over whom I have made you king , | 'Because this was in your heart... you have asked for wisdom and knowledge' — heart named; the knowing is heart-located |

**Other verses related to the context:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2Ch 1:10 | H4093 mad.da | 2Ch 1:10 Give me now wisdom and knowledge to go out and come in before this people , for who can govern this people of yours, which is so great ?” | 'Give me now wisdom and knowledge to go out and come in before this people' — mad.da requested alongside wisdom for the purpose of governance; held cognitive capacity for leadership |

## §2.9 `BOUNDARY` — Functional, supporting, and cluster-reassignment candidates

_Terms that carry inner-being relevance in their confirmed verses but do not carry an inner characteristic as their primary semantic load: functional roles (translation, arbitration, teaching), formative activities (training), speech acts (insisting), comparators (resembling), or terms flagged for cluster reassignment (see DIR-20260508-002)._

1. Terms in sub-group (13): G1128 gumnazō, G1226 diabebaioō, G1231 diaginōskō, G1256 dialegō, G1328 diermēneutēs, G1503 eikō, G2058 hermēneia, G3056 logos, G3177 methermēneuō, G3312 meristēs, G4894 suneidō, H6592 pe.sher, H8637 tir.gal
2. Verse-context groups in sub-group (13):

### §2.9.1 Group `M15-B-VCG03` (id=3646) — G4894 suneidō

_The term names understanding as a constituted inner quality that grasps, discerns, and perceives — in leadership, wisdom literature, practical navigation of situations, and the moral life. The person of understanding reads situations rightly, receives instruction, governs speech, sees through pretension, perceives the rights of others, and is responsive to correction. Inner-being phenomenon: the exercise and possession of the perceptive faculty._

### §2.9.2 Group `M15-B-VCG03` (id=3646) — G3177 methermēneuō

_The term names understanding as a constituted inner quality that grasps, discerns, and perceives — in leadership, wisdom literature, practical navigation of situations, and the moral life. The person of understanding reads situations rightly, receives instruction, governs speech, sees through pretension, perceives the rights of others, and is responsive to correction. Inner-being phenomenon: the exercise and possession of the perceptive faculty._

### §2.9.3 Group `M15-B-VCG03` (id=3646) — G2058 hermēneia

_The term names understanding as a constituted inner quality that grasps, discerns, and perceives — in leadership, wisdom literature, practical navigation of situations, and the moral life. The person of understanding reads situations rightly, receives instruction, governs speech, sees through pretension, perceives the rights of others, and is responsive to correction. Inner-being phenomenon: the exercise and possession of the perceptive faculty._

### §2.9.4 Group `M15-B-VCG03` (id=3646) — G1328 diermēneutēs

_The term names understanding as a constituted inner quality that grasps, discerns, and perceives — in leadership, wisdom literature, practical navigation of situations, and the moral life. The person of understanding reads situations rightly, receives instruction, governs speech, sees through pretension, perceives the rights of others, and is responsive to correction. Inner-being phenomenon: the exercise and possession of the perceptive faculty._

### §2.9.5 Group `M15-B-VCG03` (id=3646) — H6592 pe.sher

_The term names understanding as a constituted inner quality that grasps, discerns, and perceives — in leadership, wisdom literature, practical navigation of situations, and the moral life. The person of understanding reads situations rightly, receives instruction, governs speech, sees through pretension, perceives the rights of others, and is responsive to correction. Inner-being phenomenon: the exercise and possession of the perceptive faculty._

**Verses:** 161 connected (1 anchor, 160 other)

### §2.9.6 Group `M15-B-VCG03` (id=3646) — G1226 diabebaioō

_The term names understanding as a constituted inner quality that grasps, discerns, and perceives — in leadership, wisdom literature, practical navigation of situations, and the moral life. The person of understanding reads situations rightly, receives instruction, governs speech, sees through pretension, perceives the rights of others, and is responsive to correction. Inner-being phenomenon: the exercise and possession of the perceptive faculty._

### §2.9.7 Group `M15-B-VCG03` (id=3646) — G1503 eikō

_The term names understanding as a constituted inner quality that grasps, discerns, and perceives — in leadership, wisdom literature, practical navigation of situations, and the moral life. The person of understanding reads situations rightly, receives instruction, governs speech, sees through pretension, perceives the rights of others, and is responsive to correction. Inner-being phenomenon: the exercise and possession of the perceptive faculty._

### §2.9.8 Group `M15-B-VCG05` (id=3648) — G1128 gumnazō

_The term names understanding as an inner capacity shaped through repeated practice and sustained discipline — the formation of discernment through habitual exercise. Both positive formation (toward godliness, toward righteousness) and negative formation (hearts trained in greed) appear. Inner-being phenomenon: habituated inner formation._

**Verses:** 4 connected (1 anchor, 3 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Heb 5:14** | G1128 gumnazō | Heb 5:14 But solid food is for the mature , for those who have their powers of discernment trained by constant practice to distinguish good from evil . |  |

**Other verses related to the context:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1Ti 4:7 | G1128 gumnazō | 1Ti 4:7 Have nothing to do with irreverent , silly myths . Rather train yourself for godliness ; |  |
| Heb 12:11 | G1128 gumnazō | Heb 12:11 For the moment all discipline seems painful rather than pleasant , but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it . |  |
| 2Pe 2:14 | G1128 gumnazō | 2Pe 2:14 They have eyes full of adultery , insatiable for sin . They entice unsteady souls . They have hearts trained in greed . Accursed children ! |  |

### §2.9.9 Group `M15-B-VCG07` (id=3650) — G1256 dialegō

_The term names sustained reasoned argument directed at persuading the inner person — the systematic engagement of the inner faculties through Scripture-based discourse. The dialegō pattern of Paul's synagogue ministry is the centre: going in, reasoning, persuading. The goal is always to reach the inner life through argument. Inner-being phenomenon: inner-life engagement through reasoned discourse._

**Verses:** 11 connected (1 anchor, 10 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| **Act 24:25** | G1256 dialegō | Act 24:25 And as he reasoned about righteousness and self-control and the coming judgment , Felix was alarmed and said , “ Go away for the present . When I get an opportunity I will summon you .” |  |

### §2.9.10 Group `M15-H-VCG01` (id=3685) — G3056 logos

_The term names logos as the active divine or apostolic word that engages the inner person — the word of the cross that is folly or power depending on the inner condition of the hearer, the word of truth that produces salvation, the word of Christ dwelling richly within, the word of reconciliation entrusted to proclamation, the word of God whose integrity cannot fail. Inner-being phenomenon: the word as inner-life-addressing disclosure._

**Verses:** 19 connected (1 anchor, 18 other)

### §2.9.11 Group `M15-H-VCG02` (id=3686) — G3056 logos

_The term names logos as the communicative act of the human person — evaluated by whether it is intelligible (reaching the inner person of the hearer), gracious and seasoned (shaping the encounter), consistent with deeds, or alternatively empty, arrogant, and inconsistent. The word-as-speech is the outward expression of the inner person and is evaluated by what inner reality it carries. Inner-being phenomenon: speech as the outward expression of inner quality._

### §2.9.12 Group `M15-H-VCG03` (id=3687) — G3056 logos

_The term names logos as the single moral principle that holds and summarises all the law's content — the whole law is fulfilled in one word: love your neighbour. The logos here is not a speech-act or a divine disclosure but an inner moral principle of such compression and completeness that it contains all specific commandments. Inner-being phenomenon: the word as comprehensive inner moral standard._

**Verses:** 2 connected (1 anchor, 1 other)  

**Anchor verse:**

| Reference | Term | Verse text | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gal 5:14 | G3056 logos | Gal 5:14 For the whole law is fulfilled in one word : “You shall love your neighbor as yourself .” |  |

### §2.9.13 Group `M15-BOUNDARY-VCG01` (id=3688) — G1256 dialegō

_Jude 9: Michael contending with the devil in disputation about the body of Moses. The dialegō here is the form taken by contested engagement between spiritual beings — reasoned disputation as the mode of serious inner-faculty engagement even in angelic conflict. P-status: borderline._

**Verses:** 1 connected (1 anchor, 0 other)
